title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. X' is a (probably orbifold) curve, and G' is a group acting on it. pi_1 is the fundamental group of X'. E' is the extension 1 -> pi_1 -> E' -> G' -> 1 defined by the lifted action on the universal cover X~'. J is a set of base points stable under G', possibly including points at infinity or tangential base points. X~'(J) denotes the fibre of X~' -> X' over J. It is a set over J with a free right pi_1-action, transitive on each fibre X~'(j). It also carries a left E'-action compatible with the G'-action on J. Grothendieck calls the whole package the 'données de E''.

Item (7) aims to rebuild two things from (E', its action on X~'(J), and the map X~'(J) -> J) alone: the fundamental groupoid Pi_1(X';J) with object set J, and the G'-action on it. In brackets he first lists the 'applications (7)(8)':
- Psi^infty : X~'(J) -> Spl Ext(E'/G')/pi_1, i.e. to splittings of the extension modulo pi_1-conjugacy;
- Psi_j : X~'(j) -> Spl Ext(E'_j/G'_j), where G'_j is the stabiliser of j and E'_j its inverse image in E'.
A margin note then says these need not be given, since they follow from the other data. Indeed, the stabiliser of xi in E'_j meets pi_1 trivially (the action is free) and maps onto G'_j (the action is transitive on the fibre). So it is the image of a section of E'_j -> G'_j. This is the discrete, topological prototype of 'a point gives a section, up to conjugacy'.

NB on this page:
- For xi in X~'(j), the universal cover X~'[j] based at j (paths from j) is identified with X~' via a cover isomorphism phi_xi : X~' -> X~'[j] over X', sending xi to the constant path.
- Changing xi by gamma in pi_1 gives phi_{gamma.xi} = phi_xi o gamma_{X~'}.
- Hence there is a canonical, choice-free isomorphism X~'(j) wedge_{pi_1} X~' -> X~'[j], the contracted product of the right pi_1-torsor X~'(j) with X~'.

Next page: Isom_{Pi_1}(j,j') = Isom(X~'[j], X~'[j']) = Isom_{right pi_1-torsors}(X~'(j), X~'(j')), with composition of paths matching composition of torsor isomorphisms. The G'-action is then obtained by twisting with the pi_1-bitorsors B_g (the inverse image of g in E'), via X~'(gj) = X~'(j) wedge_{pi_1} B_g.

In short, this is the classical equivalence between 'groupoid with G'-action' and 'extension E' plus E'-set over J'. It is the multi-base-point version of the dictionary between outer actions and group extensions, as in Galois categories with several fibre functors.
errors: Left/right convention slip: he writes gamma.xi (left notation) for what the next page calls a free RIGHT pi_1-action on X~'(J). With the right action, phi_{xi gamma} = phi_xi o gamma_{X~'} is consistent with the contracted product X~'(j) x^{pi_1} X~'. Only conventions are affected, not the content.
The symbol written 'Pi_1' in 'gamma in Pi_1' and 'wedge_{Pi_1}' must be the group pi_1, not the groupoid.
The page itself gives no justification for the margin claim that the Psi maps are redundant. It is true via stabilisers in E', as explained in the reconstruction.

ideas.what: Reconstructing the fundamental groupoid on a set J of base points as the groupoid of isomorphisms between the fibre torsors X~'(j) of the universal cover.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid as the groupoid of fibre functors / torsor isomorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 Exp. V, several fibre functors); Brown for groupoids in topology
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V; the fundamental groupoid with many base points is advocated in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: The G'-action on Pi_1(X';J) is equivalent to the extension E' of G' by pi_1 together with E' acting on the fibre over J; g acts by twisting with the pi_1-bitorsor B_g.
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence between group actions on groupoids and extensions / bitorsor (2-group) descriptions
ideas.where_published: Bitorsor formalism appears in Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne and SGA-era texts; not this specific application

ideas.what: Maps from fibre points over fixed or base points to splittings of E'_j -> G'_j modulo pi_1-conjugacy, noted as determined by the E'-action (via stabilisers).
ideas.modern_name: Discrete or topological analogue of the section map (points give sections of the fundamental extension); fixed points of finite group actions give conjugacy classes of splittings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for Fuchsian groups and orbifolds; arithmetic version is Grothendieck's section conjecture (letter to Faltings 1983)
ideas.where_published: Arithmetic version in the 1983 letter to Faltings; discrete version not published by him

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of standard torsor and extension formalism for fundamental groupoids with several base points under a group action. It is a useful view of how the Teichmüller-tower framework was set up in 1980-81, but it contains nothing beyond known theory.
transcription_corrections: Line 5: read 'de E' sur X~'(J) et X~'(J) -> J'. The image shows J (bracket-like letter), consistent with Pi_1(X';J); the transcription's I appears erroneous.
Read 'Ob Pi_1 = J' (not I), consistent with the next page 'J = Ob Pi_1'.
Bracketed maps: the second reads 'Psi_j : (X~'(j) -> Spl Ext(E'_j/G'_j))', with index j (not i). The superscript on the first Psi is unclear; 'Psi^infty' is uncertain.
Margin note likely reads 'inutile de les donner, elles résultent des autres données'.
'un isomorphisme de X~' au dessus de xi' should probably be 'au dessus de X'' (an isomorphism of covers over X').
